fig1_running_couplings.svg: Running couplings from the module's closed forms. The QED fine-structure constant $\alpha(Q)$ (qed_running_alpha / qed_alpha_sm) GROWS toward high energy — vacuum-polarization screening, $\beta>0$ — climbing from $\alpha\simeq1/137$ at low $Q$ to $\simeq1/128$ at $M_Z$ once all charged Standard-Model fermions are summed. The QCD coupling $\alpha_s(Q)$ (qcd_running_alpha) instead SHRINKS with energy: asymptotic freedom, the opposite-sign $\beta<0$.
fig2_fixed_point.svg: Toy renormalization-group flow from beta_toy$(g)=a g^2-b g^3$ ($a=2,b=4$). The beta function vanishes at two fixed points (fixed_point): the Gaussian one $g=0$ (open, UV-repulsive) and $g_*=a/b=0.5$ (filled, UV-attractive). Because $dg/d\ln\mu=\beta$, the flow arrows point toward $g_*$ from both sides; the slope there, $\beta'(g_*)=-a^2/b<0$, is the linearized RG eigenvalue — the same object that fixes the critical exponents of statistical mechanics.
